text:
opsbot: ALERT 3640000123 — continuous-batching path (runtime pool-3, us-west1) p99 latency spike detected, automated pager triggered. initial anomaly window: 2026-03-15T09:12Z.

anna: I'm taking primary. pinging infra and ml oncall. how bad are token latencies?

devon: p50 fine, p95 jumped from 120ms -> 900ms, p99 > 2.5s. queue depth on pool-3 up x6, microbatch sizes showing long tails (some >256 tokens) and kv-cache hit-rate collapsed from ~98% -> ~42%. looks like prefix-KV blowup + batch coalescing jitter.

kevin: seeing repeated KV write storms in the tail — eviction churn skyrocketing. suspect prefetch heuristic interacting poorly with sudden concurrency increase from a customer load test.

anna: customer-impact? any 5xxs surfaced?

customer-support: a small set of customers (~5 tenants) reported timeouts and degraded UX on chat endpoints starting ~09:10Z. nothing widespread yet but SLAs may be impacted for those tenants.

sami: can we do a quick mitigation: reduce max_microbatch and disable aggressive prefetch for affected pool? that should collapse coalescing and stop kv fanout.

devon: agreed. plan: 1) set runtime flag max_microbatch=4 for pool-3 canary (10% nodes). 2) disable prefix prefetch for models with high KV fanout. 3) if still bad, force a soft-eviction sweep.

anna: applying canary now. command: ```
# set microbatch cap (canary)
curl -X POST https://runtime-api.internal/v1/pools/pool-3/flags 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $RUNTIME_TOKEN' 
  -d '{"max_microbatch":4,"prefetch_enabled":false}'
```

infra-bot: rollout started -> pool-3-canary (2 nodes). health checks passing.

devon: metrics after canary (5m): queue depth down ~40%, p95 halved, kv insert rate down 70%, cache hit-rate recovering to ~78%. no 5xxs from canary users.

kevin: rolling to 50% nodes now. patch: kubectl patch job/continuous-batcher -n runtime --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/0/value","value":"4"}]'

anna: rolling to 100%. watching.

infra-bot: rollout 100% complete. all health checks green.

customer-support: affected tenants reporting recovery ~2m after final rollout. one tenant reported a single timed-out request still in logs, otherwise OK.

sami: note: disabling prefetch increases per-request CPU for some hot prefixes. we need to monitor unit cost. recommend re-evaluating prefetch policy after traffic normalizes.

devon: root-cause hypothesis: a synthetic load spike caused microbatch coalescer to generate large uneven microbatches while prefix prefetch aggressively populated KV entries for many short-lived prefixes, causing eviction churn and IO latencies. combined effect produced queueing and p99 cliffs.

anna: immediate customer impact mitigated. assigning postmortem owner: devon. follow-ups: metric dashboards for kv insert/evict, add safe-guards to prefetch (rate-limit by prefix cardinality), add automatic microbatch cap when kv evict rate crosses threshold, update runbook.

kevin: quick note for ops: add a soft alarm on KV evict/sec > 1000 that auto-triggers microbatch cap to 4 for 5m.

devon: creating ticket INFRA-7263 with timeline and action items.

anna: thanks team. if anything new pops up re-open this thread. otherwise we'll post postmortem in incidents once analysis done.

opsbot: INCIDENT 3640000123 status -> RESOLVED (mitigated, monitoring).
